A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.4–4.7 and Tables 1–4 report original alignment experiments, baseline comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix C adds evaluations of IPA on InternVL3-14B and Qwen2.5VL-72B.

M1.justification: The sampling, reflective revision, instruction-oriented verification, three-round preference collection, and DPO procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C applies the existing approach to additional models.

E1.justification: The training sources in Section 3.4 and nine evaluation benchmarks in Section 4.2 are retained. Appendix C explicitly reuses the existing training dataset and evaluates the same tasks; additional model configurations do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 5 adds unaligned InternVL3-14B and Qwen2.5VL-72B as baselines against their IPA-aligned counterparts. The comparator sets in the original Tables 1, 2, and 4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds alignment and evaluation configurations using 14B and 72B models, extending the previous 7B target-model experiments. Previously reported training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3's component and collection-round ablations, Section 4.7's LLaVA filtering analysis, and Appendix B's qualitative cases are retained. The new larger-model table supplies additional standard benchmark evaluations without introducing a distinct ablation, perturbation test, or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experiments. New Table 5 follows the existing practice of reporting point scores and differences.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–4 retain identical results. New Table 5 extends the results to two larger models: InternVL3-14B's MMVet score increases from 73.0 to 75.3 with IPA, and Qwen2.5VL-72B's HallBench score increases from 55.3 to 58.4, while its MMStar score decreases from 71.6 to 71.5. These are newly reported comparisons, not revisions to earlier scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), preference-set definitions, and the mathematical description of progressive collection are retained. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about scalable instruction-oriented preference construction and improved multimodal comprehension. The added experiments provide further supporting evidence without revising those core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the larger-model results as evidence of transfer across scales and architectures, attributes more moderate improvements to stronger baselines, and suggests using stronger models for data collection. Existing interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract declares the IPA dataset publicly available and provides a Hugging Face access link, absent from v1. Appendix C specifies reuse of the existing training dataset. The optimizer settings and prompt templates are unchanged; external availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 82 reference entries are retained. Changes to citation-page backreferences reflect pagination rather than additions to research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds Appendix C.1 and a dataset-availability sentence, updates an author affiliation, and identifies corresponding authors. Existing scientific prose and section ordering remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the larger-model results table as Table 5 and renumbers the unchanged prompt tables from 5–7 to 6–8. Figure 2 and several existing tables move, and the appendices begin on a separate page. Existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 5 adds useful evidence that preferences constructed with a 7B model can benefit substantially larger models, and the dataset access statement improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are incremental. Integration remains imperfect: the unchanged conclusion still presents large-model applications as future work, and Appendix C's consistent-gains wording overlooks the MMStar decrease. Unchanged uncertainty-reporting limitations also constrain interpretation of small gains.
